\subsection{L-separation}\label{LsepV}
For $\V$-functors $f,g:Z\to X$ we write $f\cong g$ if $f\le g$ and $g\le f$; equivalently, if $f^*=g^*$, or $f_*=g_*$. We call $X$ \emph{L-separated} if $f\cong g$ implies $f=g$, for all $f,g:Z\to X$. The full subcategory of $\Cat{\V}$ consisting of all L-separated $\V$-categories is denoted by $\CatSep{\V}$. Obviously, it suffices to consider $Z=E$ (the $\otimes$-neutral object) here: writing $x:E\to X$ in $\Cat{\V}$ instead of $x\in X$, we just note that $f_*=g_*$ implies
\[
(f\cdot x)_*=f_*\cdot x_*=g_*\cdot x_*=(g\cdot x)_*.
\]
This proves the equivalence of (i),(ii) of the following proposition.
